identity.name: assert_engine_health
identity.description: CQA Tier 3: queries pg_stat_user_tables for every public-schema table (discovered at runtime, no hardcoded list) to detect dead-tuple buildup, sequential-scan dominance, and update ping-pong; snapshots the result into engine_health_snapshots (one guarded-upsert row per table, per day) and auto-VACUUM ANALYZEs tables above the dead-tuple threshold. Runs in all 4 chains (permits/coa/sources/deep_scrapes) plus standalone. Re-derived from ASSERT to RECORDER (operator ruling 2026-09-14, report §2): the engine_health_snapshots write is a genuine 6-column IS-DISTINCT-FROM-guarded upsert with no legal home under ASSERT's forced outputs:"none", and no threshold in this file has ever reached the halt.

why_lock.text: Registered in Spec 47 §A.5 (docs/specs/01-pipeline/47_pipeline_script_protocol.md:1948), category "6 — Quality", writes-DB column reads "NO — snapshot recording" — the registry's own pre-existing framing already read this step's write as recording, supporting the RECORDER ruling. Kept via identity.lock + the §5.4 source-text convention (ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 104 declared, never read, in the frozen shell).

idempotent_rerun_why.text: pg_stat_user_tables counters (seq_scan/idx_scan/n_tup_ins/n_tup_upd) are cumulative and monotonically increase with ANY query activity against the target table, including this step's own reads of pg_stat_user_tables and its own snapshot upserts — so two back-to-back runs will almost always show real drift on at least seq_scan/idx_scan, even with zero application traffic in between. The 6-column IS DISTINCT FROM guard exists to skip the rows that happen to be genuinely unchanged (report §2.2 item 2: more disciplined than the refresh_snapshot exemplar's own guard:"none"), not to guarantee a zero-write re-run generally.

guard_columns_why.text: LG-9 escape hatch, moot here — guard_columns is only consulted to build the IS DISTINCT FROM clause when guard != "none", and "all_declared" resolves to exactly the 6 columns[] entries above, none of which is a run_at-sourced column (captured_at is a bookkeeping timestamp stamped by the write statement's own SET clause, not declared in columns[] — same convention refresh_snapshot's own created_at uses).

why.text: One INSERT...ON CONFLICT (table_name, snapshot_date) DO UPDATE per discovered table, each statement autocommitted independently (no explicit BEGIN/COMMIT anywhere in the pre-conversion file, preserved verbatim) — write_inventory.statements counts the ONE distinct statement TEXT (UPSERT_SQL), executed once per row in the compute-owned loop, not once per invocation. The 6-column IS DISTINCT FROM guard is genuinely more disciplined than the RECORDER exemplar's own guard:"none" (report §2.2 item 2, §4.1 CONTRACT).

ONE write statement — the single INSERT...ON CONFLICT (table_name, snapshot_date) DO UPDATE (UPSERT_SQL) — executed once per table pg_stat_user_tables discovers at runtime (today ~40+ rows per run), never batched into a single multi-row statement. write_inventory.statements counts distinct WRITE statement forms per step.schema.json's own convention (refresh_snapshot's identical framing), not invocation count.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value this compute already measured (tableResults / insp / coa) — a check that throws is a library-or-compute defect, not an upstream condition. It must redden the run, not drop its row.

expect.reports: count of tables (live >= engine_health_dead_tuple_min_rows) whose dead-tuple ratio exceeds engine_health_dead_tuple_ratio_warn_max

why.text: Ported by predicate from the pre-conversion file's generic per-table loop (:118-124, DEAD_TUPLE_RATIO=0.10). Never blocking — report §1.2 measured this threshold never reached the halt; declaring severity:FAIL here (rather than WARN) would introduce a real halt (RUN_STATUS.FAILED) this step never had. The `live >= 1000` floor (R1, review panel commit 7 → peel commit 8, report §9.6) was itself a bare literal until this peel — externalized as engine_health_dead_tuple_min_rows below (byte-identical default 1000), the same convention seq_scan_ratio_high's own min-rows floor already used.

expect.reports: count of tables (live >= engine_health_seq_scan_min_rows) whose sequential-scan ratio exceeds engine_health_seq_scan_ratio_warn_max

why.text: Ported by predicate from the pre-conversion file's generic per-table loop (:127-132, SEQ_SCAN_RATIO=0.80, SEQ_SCAN_MIN_ROWS=10000).

expect.reports: count of tables whose cumulative update/insert ratio exceeds engine_health_ping_pong_ratio_warn_max

why.text: Ported by predicate from the pre-conversion file's generic per-table loop (:134-139, PING_PONG_RATIO=10 — AEH-IL-1: raised from 2 to 10 at 8c9e64d7, 2026-03-21, because dimensional tables naturally run 5-6x and the spec's own >2x bound produced chronic false-positive WARNs; Spec 41's table still declares >2x, a spec-vs-code drift named at commit 1, resolved at commit 9's spec-diff, not silently here).

AEH-IL-5. Pre-conversion inspAuditTable (Phase 6, deep_scrapes-only) displayed this predicate as status:'FAIL' text (:222), but no threshold in the file — including this one — ever reached the halt (report §1.2, exhaustively measured: the ONLY throw site is the outer catch on a genuine exception). Declaring severity:"FAIL" here would introduce a REAL halt (RUN_STATUS.FAILED) this step never had — a genuine regression, not a verbatim port — so this check is declared WARN, resolving AEH-D3's FAIL-vs-WARN inconsistency (both insp and coa variants below now agree) rather than preserving the cosmetic label.

AEH-IL-5/AEH-D3. Pre-conversion :223 disagreed with the top-level PING_PONG_RATIO=10 for the conceptually same update/insert-ratio metric (5x vs 10x) — this session's own finding, not silently unified: kept as its OWN distinct logic variable (engine_health_insp_update_insert_fail_ratio) rather than folded into engine_health_ping_pong_ratio_warn_max, since the two may legitimately want different sensitivity for one table vs the whole fleet (report §5 low-confidence #2). Never blocking, same reasoning as insp_dead_tuple_pct above.

AEH-IL-6. Pre-conversion coaAuditTable (Phase 9, coa-only) used the IDENTICAL 10% bound as insp_dead_tuple_pct's own predicate (:255) but WARN severity, not FAIL — the two per-chain audit tables already disagreed only on severity, never on value. This check reuses engine_health_insp_dead_tuple_fail_pct's VALUE (per AEH-IL-6's own disposition: "the SAME logic var ... with its OWN severity declared explicitly") rather than declaring a 7th variable for an identical bound.

invariants.sql: SELECT count(*)::int AS c FROM (SELECT table_name, snapshot_date FROM engine_health_snapshots GROUP BY table_name, snapshot_date HAVING count(*) > 1) d

why.text: Mirrors the live UNIQUE(table_name, snapshot_date) DB constraint as a declared, observable check rather than an implicit reliance on the constraint alone (Rule 1, nothing hidden) — same convention refresh_snapshot's own duplicate_snapshot_date_count invariant uses.

This step's VACUUM ANALYZE target set (vacuumTargets) is discovered AT RUNTIME from pg_stat_user_tables, not enumerable at descriptor-authoring time as execution.maintenance's array requires (one row per NAMED table) — forcing a static enumeration would silently reintroduce the hardcoded-list defect the step's own design explicitly rejects (:72-79, "Discover all public-schema tables dynamically — no hardcoded list"). Ask 2 / Fold 1 (binding, .cursor/batch1_i3_assert_engine_health_active_task.md): keep the chain-tail VACUUM loop verbatim, compute-owned, declared here via deviations[] rather than execution.maintenance — the SAME mechanism EP-D17's 2026-09-10 DEFER already established for this exact file (review_followups.md:3480: "do NOT hoist the vacuum decision into the chain head, do NOT touch assert-engine-health.js or run-chain.js beyond the telemetry fold"). Spec 43 (:142,:150) independently names this file as the deliberate, still-OPEN "chain-tail VACUUM owner".

runRecorderPhase (scripts/lib/step/index.js) mechanically supports exactly ONE write statement per run (one buildRow/buildWriteSql/executeRecorderUpsert call) — this step's real write is N rows (one per runtime-discovered table) plus a separate VACUUM maintenance loop, a shape runRecorderPhase cannot express without a runtime-library change (a RE-FREEZE decision, out of this commit's authority per Operating Boundaries — step.schema.json is frozen). Leaving execution.shape undeclared matches the pattern the 3 live ASSERT descriptors already use (assert-data-bounds/assert-schema/assert-global-coverage): none of isIngestStep/isLinkStep/…/isRecorderStep/isEnrichStep match an undeclared shape (only isIngestStep keeps a legacy structural inference, gated on an external URL read this step has none of), so the runtime falls through to calling compute(ctx) directly with full ctx.pool access — exactly what this step's self-managed reads/writes/VACUUM loop needs. identity.archetype stays "RECORDER" (the operator's classification ruling); execution.shape is a separate, runtime-EXECUTION axis neither the red suite nor R-PACE-1's archetype-eligibility count reads.

deviations.adjudicated_by: This commit (batch1 I3 commit 7) — a newly-measured architecture finding, reported rather than silently worked around; not yet operator-ratified as a general pattern.

AEH-D3's original finding (FAIL vs WARN for the identical predicate) is therefore RESOLVED by this commit, not merely preserved — a deliberate call made to avoid introducing a genuine halt-on-FAIL regression, reported here rather than left for a later commit.
limitations.measured: report §1.2 (exhaustive halt-path trace) + this commit's own re-derivation, both cited in checks[].why for insp_dead_tuple_pct/coa_dead_tuple_pct above.

limitations.what: The insp/coa targeted follow-up queries (fetchInsUpdVac) now run ONLY when the corresponding chain's check is actually selected (ctx.checks), rather than unconditionally on every chain as the pre-conversion file did (:208-211/:242-245 ran regardless of CHAIN_ID; only the DISPLAY was chain-scoped). The reported values are identical when they run — this eliminates 1-2 wasted queries per invocation on chains that never displayed the result.
limitations.measured: Pre-conversion :200-266 built both inspAuditTable and coaAuditTable unconditionally on every chain if the respective table row existed; only the meta-object IIFE (:278-293) selected which ONE to display.

limitations.what: execution.shape is left UNDECLARED (not "recorder") — this step's real write is N rows over a runtime-discovered table set plus a VACUUM maintenance loop, a shape runRecorderPhase cannot express (report §9.1). Restated here (R3, commit 8 peel) so the fact is visible wherever limitations[]/deviations[] are rendered (registry, step-validate --write), not deviations[]-prose-only.
limitations.measured: report §9.1; deviations[] entry "execution.shape — left undeclared rather than \"recorder\"" above carries the full grounds.

recovery.reset: Re-running recomputes every table's live pg_stat_user_tables snapshot from scratch; the 6-column IS DISTINCT FROM guard only rewrites rows whose stats actually changed since the last capture, which IS the correct, and only, reset mechanism — there is no history to rebuild, every value is a fresh point-in-time read.

interrupted_why.text: retract:"none" on the one write target — there is nothing for an interrupted run to leave half-retracted. A crashed mid-loop run simply leaves some tables' rows stale (or absent, for a brand-new table) until the next run recomputes them fresh; a re-run is the same normal-run behaviour, not a special recovery path.

before_image_why.text: R-M's scope is destructive retraction (a DELETE, or an overwrite whose prior value cannot be re-derived) — this write is an idempotent keyed upsert, retract:"none", every column re-derived FRESH from the live pg_stat_user_tables catalog on every run. A stored snapshot row is itself just a point-in-time capture of a PRIOR live state, not a source of truth a before-image would protect; a re-run recovers identically to what a before-image could restore.

why.text: The normal, and only steady-state, outcome: every table is re-recorded every run. Verdict is PASS when no declared check reports a violation.

One or more declared checks report a WARN (a threshold breach, a write/VACUUM failure) and nothing FAILED — the run completed and wrote every table's row; the warning is in the table. All 8 declared checks are severity WARN by design (report §1.2 — no threshold in this step has ever halted anything).
Advisory lock 104 is held by another process — a row-derived SKIP summary, never a bare SDK skip with no audit_table.
One of the 6 declared logic_variables resolved outside its bounds under on_invalid:"fail". hoisted_above_gate puts this refusal ABOVE the advisory lock.

A genuine uncaught exception (DB connectivity, a malformed query in the table-discovery or stat-scan reads) — the ONLY thing that has ever halted this step (report §1.2). The per-table VACUUM and snapshot-write loops are NOT this terminal's trigger — both are non-fatal by design (engine_health_vacuum_failed / engine_health_write_failed WARN checks instead).
